feed.title: NPR Topics: National
feed.subtitle: NPR coverage of national news, U.S. politics, elections, business, arts, culture, health and science, and technology. Subscribe to the NPR Nation RSS feed.

entry.title: New space station crew launches from Florida on SpaceX's Crew Dragon capsule
entry.summary: The crew of four — two NASA astronauts, one from Canada, and a Russian cosmonaut — heads to the International Space Station after liftoff from the Cape Canaveral Space Force Station in Florida.

entry.title: Studying this super El Niño could save lives. NOAA is scaling back research
entry.summary: A powerful El Niño is already influencing extreme weather around the planet. During the last strong El Niño, federal agencies ramped up research in the hope of improving weather forecasts. This year, they won't be matching that effort.

entry.title: Do AI and air traffic control mix? CEO addresses anxiety about new FAA tool
entry.summary: The FAA's ambitious overhaul of the air traffic control system comes amid rising public anxiety about AI. The CEO of the company that's building the software explains how it works.

entry.title: SNAP's funding model is starting to change. Here's what that means for the program
entry.summary: States will start to pay a larger share of the bill to run the food assistance program, as federal funding for operational costs shrinks.

entry.title: Egg prices have tumbled since Trump returned to office. Here's why
entry.summary: Agriculture experts say high egg prices were the result of severe avian flu outbreaks, but the Trump administration's tariffs and the war with Iran have also put pressure on farmers.

entry.title: Trump administration reverses stance on integration of people with disabilities
entry.summary: Disability rights advocates are angered by the latest reversal but are rallying behind proposed legislation and working with states to strengthen protections for community integration.

entry.title: Along U.S. Route 1, Maine voters worry about heating oil, gas and Canadian tariffs
entry.summary: Home to both Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson, Maine's senate race has put rural Aroostook County in the spotlight.

entry.title: Leaning into culture war flashpoints, Hegseth announces new Pentagon initiatives
entry.summary: In an address to troops, Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth leaned hard into culture war flashpoints, while touting new military initiatives.

entry.title: Tennessee governor halts executions after Christa Gail Pike survives lethal injection
entry.summary: Tennessee officials were unable to put Christa Gail Pike to death Wednesday for a 1995 murder after administering two doses of a lethal drug. Tennessee Gov. Bill Lee halted the remaining execution for the year.

entry.title: Leaning into culture war flashpoints, Hegseth says he has transformed U.S. military
entry.summary: Secretary of Defense Pete Hegseth told hundreds of junior military officers and enlisted leaders on Wednesday that the Trump administration has achieved a cultural shift in the military.
